LEHI, Utah--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Huckleberry.ai, Inc. (formerly Domo, Inc.) CITY OF INDUSTRY, Calif., Nov. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Celebrating 40 years of GIGABYTE, GIGABYTE has partnered with Newegg to host AORUS VS40, a free community gaming celebration taking place on Saturday, November 21, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. PST at the Newegg Gamer Zone in Diamond Bar, California. The event invites local collegiate PC gamers, esports fans, and hardware enthusiasts to mark GIGABYTE's 40-year milestone with competitive esports tournaments, hands-on hardware challenges, and exclusive gear.

Under the theme "PLAY. WIN. MAKE IT YOURS.", AORUS VS40 features high-energy 1v1 competitions in VALORANT and League of Legends. To deliver peak competitive performance on the main stage, all tournament rigs are powered by GIGABYTE's flagship AMD X870 motherboards and premium AMD Radeon graphics cards. The setups allow players to experience seamless gameplay, maximum frame rates, and low-latency response times during high-stakes tournament matches.

Beyond the competitive arena, attendees can explore interactive gaming stations throughout the venue. Visitors can test their response times in speed challenges on high-refresh GIGABYTE gaming monitors, get hands-on experience with the latest GIGABYTE gaming laptops, and participate in an event passport stamp activity to earn exclusive prizes. Additional event highlights include a custom tote bag heat-press station, hourly raffle prize drawings, limited-edition GIGABYTE 40th-anniversary merchandise, photo opportunities, and complimentary food and refreshments while supplies last.

The collaborative celebration between GIGABYTE, Newegg, and AMD reflects a shared commitment to empowering the Southern California gaming community. By bringing together top-tier hardware manufacturers and leading e-commerce platforms, AORUS VS40 offers local collegiate gamers and tech enthusiasts an immersive platform to connect, compete, and celebrate four decades of GIGABYTE's impact on PC gaming.

"At Newegg, a lot of great builds have started with GIGABYTE parts, and we're proud to celebrate GIGABYTE's 40 years in PC gaming," said Jim Tseng, Vice President of product management at Newegg. "Hosting this celebration at the Newegg Gamer Zone gives local gamers a day to compete, try the latest hardware, and take home something to remember it by."

Admission to AORUS VS40 is complimentary, but advance RSVP via Eventbrite is strictly required as capacity is limited to 250 guests on a first-come, first-served basis. Attendees are encouraged to arrive early with their Eventbrite confirmation. Guests under 18 years of age must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian, and additional age restrictions may apply to tournament participation. To reserve a spot or learn more, please visit [Eventbrite RSVP Link].

The Newegg Gamer Zone, a 2,300-square-foot gaming venue at Newegg's headquarters, hosts esports tournaments, product launches, and community events throughout the year. It is open to the public Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. PT. Walk-ins are welcome, or guests can reserve a visit. Gamers who can't attend AORUS VS40 can find the GIGABYTE motherboards, graphics cards, monitors, and laptops featured at the event at Newegg.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MetaOptics Ltd (Catalist: 9MT) (OTCQX: MOTLY) ("MetaOptics" or the "Company", and together with its subsidiaries, the "Group"), a Singapore-headquartered semiconductor optics company pioneering glass-based metalens solutions enhanced by AI-driven image processing, announced that it had on 20 November 2026, entered into a share subscription facility agreement with GEM Opportunities Fund ISA Ltd. ("GEM"), the Bermuda-based investment vehicle managed by Global Emerging Markets (GEM), New York, for an aggregate commitment of up to S$32 million (the "Share Subscription Facility"). The Share Subscription Facility is subject to, inter alia, the approval of the Company's shareholders ("Shareholders") at an extraordinary general meeting ("EGM") to be convened. A circular containing further details of the Share Subscription Facility, together with the notice of EGM, will be despatched to Shareholders in due course.

The Company intends to apply the net proceeds from drawdowns under the Share Subscription Facility, entirely for the Group's working capital purposes, including general corporate expenses, funding the day-to-day operations of the Group and supporting the growth of its existing business. As part of the Group's plans to grow its existing business, the Group intends to establish a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States to produce metalenses for co-packaged optics ("CPO") and colour imaging applications. The Share Subscription Facility provides MetaOptics with flexible access to growth capital while allowing the Company to control the timing of any drawdowns, in line with its capital needs and prevailing market conditions.

Mr Thng Chong Kim, Executive Chairman of MetaOptics, said: "This Share Subscription Facility gives us a reliable, flexible source of capital for our day-to-day operations and to support the growth of our existing business by establishing a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States, on terms that put MetaOptics in control of the timing and size of each drawdown. We are pleased to have the backing of GEM, an experienced global investor, as we execute on our plans and build long-term value for our Shareholders."

data.title: Anteris’ DurAVR THV Demonstrates 1% Heart Failure Hospitalization, Single-Digit Gradients and No Valve-Related Deaths at 1 Year in Patients with Small Aortic Annuli | AVR Stock News
data.description:

Add on Google

Late-breaking 1-year data in 100 patients presented at PCR London Valves 2026: No moderate or severe paravalvular leak, 96% in NYHA class I/II and 97% free from moderate or severe prosthesis-patient mismatch at 30 days

MINNEAPOLIS and BRISBANE, Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Anteris Technologies Global Corp. (“Anteris” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: AVR, ASX: AVR) today announced 1-year clinical and hemodynamic outcomes for the DurAVR® Transcatheter Heart Valve (THV) in 100 patients with severe aortic stenosis and small aortic annuli (annulus area 404 ± 37 mm2), the anatomy in which transcatheter valves most often leave patients with elevated gradients and prosthesis-patient mismatch* (PPM).

At 1 year, 1% of patients had been hospitalized for heart failure. DurAVR THV maintained a mean pressure gradient of 8.9 mmHg and a mean effective orifice area (EOA) of 2.2 cm2, with no moderate or severe paravalvular leak (PVL) observed and no valve-related mortality reported. At 30 days, 97% of patients were free from moderate or severe PPM. Symptoms improved substantially: the proportion of patients who achieved New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I/II rose from 39% at baseline to 96% at 1 year.

These results were achieved in a symptomatic and clinically complex population. At baseline, 61% of patients were in NYHA class III/IV, the mean STS-PROM score was 4.7 ± 4.0%, and the cohort included heavy calcification and bicuspid anatomy (9%). Patients were pooled from the EMBARK and early feasibility studies (EFS) conducted in the United States and Europe; previously, 30-day data from this cohort were presented at PCR London Valves 2025.

The late-breaking abstract, titled “One-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes of a Novel Biomimetic Balloon-Expandable THV in Small Aortic Annuli,” was presented by Rishi Puri, MD, PhD, of Cleveland Clinic, during the TAVI Hotline – Part 1 session at PCR London Valves on Sunday, November 22, 2026.

1 Year Results Highlights

  • Heart failure hospitalization: 1% at 1 year compares favorably to mid-to-high single-digit rates reported in contemporary clinical trials with currently marketed products.1,2
  • Hemodynamics: Mean pressure gradient fell from 48.1 ± 17.0 mmHg at baseline to 8.9 ± 4.3 mmHg at 1 year, and mean EOA increased from 0.8 ± 0.2 cm2 to 2.2 ± 0.9 cm2. These results were similar to those reported at 30 days in 2025.
  • Hemodynamic Valve Deterioration: No moderate or severe hemodynamic valve deterioration was observed at 1 year.
  • Valve performance: No moderate or severe PVL was observed and no valve-related deaths were reported through 1 year.
  • Symptoms: Patients in NYHA class I/II increased from 39% at baseline to 96% at 1 year, and 81% of patients experienced symptom improvement.
  • Clinical events at 1 year: All-cause mortality 6% (2 CV mortalities; 2 non-cardiac infections; 1 cancer; 1 car accident), stroke 3% and new permanent pacemaker implantation 9%.
  • Cardiac remodeling: In a cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) substudy (n = 64), left ventricular (LV) mass, a marker of modifying the underlying disease, regressed by 24% at 1 year. LV mass in the patients evaluated was similar to that reported in matched controls without aortic valve disease3. These findings are consistent with sustained unloading of the left ventricle.

“Small aortic annuli are where we most often see elevated gradients and mismatch after TAVR, and these patients are disproportionately women. In this symptomatic cohort, DurAVR delivered single-digit gradients, no moderate or greater paravalvular leak and 97% freedom from moderate or severe mismatch at 30 days. While cross-trial comparisons should be interpreted with caution, what stands out to me is heart failure hospitalization of just 1% at one year. These patients had a mean STS score of 4.7%, and most were in NYHA class III or IV, yet 1% is well below the hospitalization rates reported in contemporary clinical trials with currently marketed products. These are encouraging results, and the randomized PARADIGM trial is the right next test,” said Rishi Puri, MD, PhD, Interventional Cardiologist, Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, Ohio, United States.

“Small annuli are the hardest test in TAVR, and these patients were symptomatic, with 61% in NYHA class III or IV at baseline. At one year, heart failure hospitalization was just 1%, a fraction of the rate typically observed after valve replacement. Heart failure admissions are the event patients feel most, health systems pay for most and that most closely predicts mortality. The cardiac MRI data show why DurAVR is different: with single-digit gradients and no moderate or severe paravalvular leak, left ventricular mass regressed by 24%, which tells us the heart is unloading and beginning to remodel. We believe DurAVR's biomimetic design and its potential to restore more physiologic blood flow may contribute to improved cardiac remodeling. These findings are consistent with that hypothesis, and PARADIGM is designed to test DurAVR head-to-head against today’s commercial valves. These results give us strong conviction going into the pivotal trial,” said Chris Meduri, MD, MPH, Chief Medical Officer of Anteris.

“Reducing heart failure hospitalization is among the most consequential events after aortic valve replacement, due to its proven correlation with CV mortality. In a pooled analysis of more than 3,400 patients treated with TAVR or surgical aortic valve replacement in the PARTNER trials, the 1-year heart failure hospitalization rate was 6.7%, and these hospitalizations were associated with increased mortality.1 In the randomized SMART trial of small-annulus patients at lower predicted risk (mean STS-PROM 3.3%), 1-year heart failure hospitalization was 4.1% with the Evolut valve and 3.5% with the SAPIEN valve.2 Against this backdrop, our current dataset gives us great confidence for the ongoing pivotal PARADIGM study where cardiovascular hospitalization is also a component of the primary endpoint,” said Wayne Paterson, Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Anteris.

The DurAVR THV is being studied in the pivotal PARADIGM Trial (ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT07194265), a randomized, head-to-head comparison against commercially available TAVR valves that is actively enrolling patients across the United States and Europe.

1Huded CP, et al. Circ Cardiovasc Interv. 2022;15(12):e012195.

2Herrmann HC, et al. Self-Expanding or Balloon-Expandable TAVR in Patients with a Small Aortic Annulus. N Engl J Med. 2024;390:1959-1971. Component rates (Kaplan-Meier) from SMART results posted at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04722250.

3Garg P, et al. European Heart Journal, Valvular & Structural Disease; 2026.

*Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) occurs when an implanted valve’s effective opening is too small for the patient’s body size, resulting in higher-than-expected gradients. PPM is common after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with small aortic annuli and has been associated with reduced long-term survival after surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR).

About the PARADIGM Trial

The PARADIGM Trial is a prospective randomized controlled trial which will evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the DurAVR Transcatheter Heart Valve compared to commercially available transcatheter aortic valve replacements (TAVRs).

This head-to-head study will enroll approximately 1,000 patients in the ‘All Comers Randomized Cohort' with 1:1 randomization of patients who will receive either the DurAVR THV or TAVR using commercially available and approved THVs. The PARADIGM Trial will assess non-inferiority on a primary composite endpoint of all-cause mortality, all stroke and cardiovascular hospitalization at one year post procedure.

For further information, please refer to ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07194265.

About Anteris

Anteris Technologies Global Corp. (NASDAQ: AVR, ASX: AVR) is a global healthcare company committed to designing, developing, and commercializing cutting-edge medical devices to restore healthy heart function. Founded in Australia, with a significant presence in Minneapolis, USA, Anteris is a science-driven company with an experienced team of multidisciplinary professionals delivering restorative solutions to structural heart disease patients.

Anteris’ lead product, the DurAVR THV, was designed in collaboration with the world’s leading interventional cardiologists and cardiac surgeons to treat aortic stenosis – a potentially life-threatening condition resulting from the narrowing of the aortic valve. The balloon-expandable DurAVR THV is the first biomimetic valve, which is shaped to mimic the performance of a healthy human aortic valve and aims to replicate normal aortic blood flow. DurAVR THV is made using a single piece of molded ADAPT® tissue, Anteris’ patented anti-calcification tissue technology. ADAPT tissue, which is FDA-cleared, has been used clinically for over 10 years and distributed for use in over 55,000 patients worldwide. The DurAVR THV System is comprised of the DurAVR valve, the ADAPT tissue, and the balloon-expandable ComASUR® Delivery System.

HONG KONG and SHANGHAI and FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HUTCHMED (China) Limited (“HUTCHMED”) (Nasdaq/AIM:​HCM; HKEX:​13) today announces that it has initiated RANOVA, a registrational Phase III clinical trial of ranosidenib (HMPL-306) in patients with postoperative residual or recurrent Grade 2 gliomas harboring isocitrate dehydrogenase (“IDH”) 1 or 2 mutations in China. Ranosidenib is a novel, highly potent and selective dual inhibitor of IDH1 and IDH2 mutant enzymes. The first patient received the first dose on November 20, 2026.

Gliomas are the most common primary brain tumors, representing around 80% of all primary malignant and central nervous system tumors.1 Worldwide, it is estimated that approximately 260,000 new cases of glioma are diagnosed annually, including nearly 70,000 in China. 2,3 IDH1 or IDH2 mutations are recognized as key oncogenic drivers in the pathogenesis and progression of glioma, found in approximately 70% to 80% of Grade 2 or 3 gliomas, including astrocytoma and oligodendroglioma.4

The trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III study evaluating the efficacy and safety of oral ranosidenib versus placebo in participants with postoperative residual or recurrent Grade 2 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma carrying IDH1 or IDH2 mutations who have previously received only surgical treatment. Following Blinded Independent Review Committee (“BIRC”)-confirmed disease progression, eligible participants in the placebo group may cross over to receive ranosidenib.

The primary outcome measure is progression-free survival (“PFS”) assessed by BIRC according to Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) 2.0 criteria. Secondary outcome measures include investigator-assessed PFS, time to next intervention (TTNI), tumor growth rate (TGR), objective response rate (ORR), overall survival (OS), safety, and quality of life. Additional details may be found at clinicaltrials.gov, using identifier NCT07912398.

This registrational trial plans to enroll approximately 210 patients in China. The leading principal investigators are Professor Jinsong Wu of Huashan Hospital, Fudan University and Professor Xiaohui Ren of Capital Medical University Beijing Tiantan Hospital.

About Ranosidenib

Ranosidenib is a novel dual-inhibitor of IDH1 and IDH2 mutant enzymes. Mutations of IDH1 and IDH2 have been implicated as drivers of certain hematological malignancies, gliomas and solid tumors. Cytoplasmic mutant IDH1 and mitochondrial mutant IDH2 have been known to switch to the other form when targeted by an inhibitor of IDH1 mutant alone or IDH2 mutant alone. Targeting both IDH1 and IDH2 mutations may provide therapeutic benefits in cancer patients by overcoming this acquired resistance.

HUTCHMED currently retains all rights to ranosidenib worldwide.

About HUTCHMED

HUTCHMED (Nasdaq/AIM:HCM; HKEX:13) is an innovative, commercial-stage, biopharmaceutical company. It is committed to the discovery and global development and commercialization of targeted therapies and immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer and immunological diseases. Since inception it has focused on bringing drug candidates from in-house discovery to patients around the world, with its first five medicines marketed in China, the first of which is also approved around the world including in the US, Europe and Japan. This week, the district's career education center led the way by purchasing several robots, including FX Navi and Aegis EDU. We hope the project will serve as a model for a broader rollout across the district.

Second, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with another public school district, one of California's leading districts. The district has also purchased robot devices including Master Mini and Aegis EDU. Third, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with an additional major public school district in Los Angeles.

The second and third partnerships both cover K–12 through adult education. We'll work with the two districts to develop curricula together, set up innovation labs, create career and technical education pathways, train teachers, and give students hands-on experience. Together, we'll explore how Physical AI education can connect what students learn in the classroom with further study, real-world practice, and career development. By working with major school districts as strategic partners at the school district level, we can work directly with the U.S. public education system to build Physical AI education pathways that connect K–12 learning, technical skills training, and future careers.

NUREMBERG, Germany, Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- At SPS 2026, Schneider Electric, a global energy technology leader, will show how machine builders and industrial operators can get more from their automation, from individual machines through to production processes and plant-wide operations.

Companies have access to more operational and energy data, AI and analytics than ever before. The challenge is using that intelligence to increase productivity and efficiency on the shop floor.

On its stand, Schneider Electric will demonstrate how Industrial Intelligence and Open, Software-Defined Automation connect data and AI with machine and process control. Visitors will also see how energy and operational data can be managed together, rather than as separate challenges.

“Industrial companies don't need more data. They need the ability to turn intelligence into action,” says Gwenaelle Huet, executive vice president of Industrial Automation at Schneider Electric. “That is why we believe automation must be open and software-defined: it lets customers bring energy, AI and operations together, and keep evolving without replacing the investments they have already made.”

“SPS brings together one of the world’s most important machine-building and automation communities, at a time when companies need to be more productive and competitive,” said Jessica Bethune, vice president of Industrial and Process Automation DACH at Schneider Electric. “Machine builders need to develop differentiated machines faster and scale them more easily. Industrial operators need to improve process performance and modernize without starting from scratch.”

Advancing Open, Software-Defined Automation

At SPS, Schneider Electric will launch the newest release of EcoStruxure Automation Expert, its vendor-agnostic, software-defined automation platform. The update makes engineering simpler. It also makes it easier for customers to modernise the systems they already run and to prepare for AI-enabled automation.

New collaboration and development features reduce the time spent on engineering and integration. Support for open APIs, Visual Studio Code and Python lets engineers keep using the tools they already know.

The release also gives customers more flexibility to modernize and update critical systems while minimizing disruption to operations. A new web-native HMI enables browser-based visualization and maintenance. Expanded online-change and high-availability capabilities let systems evolve progressively, without replacing automation investments that are still viable.

More open access to automation data also makes it easier to connect external AI tools and introduce AI-assisted engineering and operations. For machine builders, this means faster engineering and greater reuse across machine portfolios. For industrial operators, it offers a practical way to add new software and intelligence capabilities as their operations evolve.

With EcoStruxure Automation Expert already deployed at more than 900 customer sites worldwide, Schneider Electric is demonstrating how open, software-defined automation runs industrial operations today.

Automate 360: enabling continuity and adoption at scale
To accelerate adoption of open, software-defined automation, we are introducing Automate 360: the unified environment and foundational layer across control and compute that underpins EcoStruxure Automation Expert. It brings project and device management, licensing, collaboration tools and cybersecurity together in one experience, with a common data space, all within a modular, scalable environment.

With Automate 360, customers can adopt EcoStruxure Automation Expert while keeping consistent, interoperable workflows and lifecycle tools across engineering and operations. It also supports their existing environments, including EcoStruxure Control Expert, Process Expert and Machine Expert.

Innovation from machine to plant

At the machine level, Schneider Electric will introduce the new Modicon M380 ePAC, bringing Modicon M580-class connectivity and cybersecurity to the Modicon M340 footprint for small to mid-sized industrial and infrastructure applications. Integrated EtherNet/IP and Modbus TCP communications, with optional OPC UA connectivity, provide easier access to operational data and a path for customers to evolve existing automation architectures.

For process and hybrid industries, Foxboro SDA, the latest Distributed Control System that integrates Automation Expert as its engineering layer, extends the same open, software-defined principles into distributed control, helping customers modernize control environments with greater flexibility while protecting existing automation investments.

Across its connected industrial powertrain portfolio, Schneider Electric will also demonstrate how energy distribution, motor control, drives, connected sensors and analytics can work together to improve energy efficiency, asset performance and predictive maintenance.

Together, these developments show how openness, intelligence, and software-defined automation can extend from machine builders designing the next generation of equipment to manufacturers optimizing complex production and process environments.

LONDON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Smartphone shipments in Africa fell 40% year-on-year (YoY) to 13.7 million units, down from 22.8 million a year earlier, according to Omdia’s latest research. This marked the steepest YoY decline in three years following three consecutive years of third-quarter growth. Rising component costs and currency pressures are changing how vendors price their devices and how consumers buy them across Africa's largest markets.

Africa smartphone market shipment, 2Q23 to 3Q26

Rising prices weigh on smartphone shipments and market value

Shipments of smartphones priced below $100 fell nearly 70% YoY in 3Q26, while feature phone shipments grew 27%. Entry-level smartphones are becoming less profitable, prompting vendors to reconsider which models they offer and how they price them. Consumers who pay in cash, particularly those without access to operator subsidies or financing, are delaying upgrades or turning to refurbished smartphones and feature phones. Higher-priced smartphones are increasingly out of reach for these buyers.

“The figures show how affordability is shaping buying decisions in Africa. Some buyers are waiting longer to upgrade or choosing a refurbished smartphone to stay within budget,” notes Manish Pravinkumar, Principal Analyst at Omdia. “In many other regions, higher average selling prices (ASPs) helped sustain market value as shipments fell. In Africa, the ASP reached $222 in 3Q26, its highest third-quarter level in a decade. Even so, market value fell 15%. The increase in average price reflects a widening affordability gap and offers little evidence that buyers are moving to more expensive models.”

Nigeria and Egypt record the steepest shipment declines among Africa’s key markets

The size of the decline varied across Africa's key markets, reflecting differences in economic conditions, access to consumer financing, and exposure to currency and policy changes. Nigeria recorded the steepest decline among these markets, with smartphone shipments down 47% YoY. Fuel price pressures following subsidy removal, limited access to US dollars for import payments and higher handset costs further reduced household purchasing power.

In Egypt, smartphone shipments fell 41%. A weaker Egyptian pound and persistent inflation raised the cost of importing phones and manufacturing them locally, prompting consumers to delay upgrades.

In Kenya, smartphone shipments fell 35%. Shipments in the country’s core price segment, smartphones priced below $150, fell 44% as higher device prices put these devices beyond the reach of more buyers. Credit purchases and instalment plans are playing a growing role in helping consumers manage upfront costs.

South Africa recorded a smaller decline of 20%. Established operator distribution networks, contract upgrades, and a wider range of retail channels helped support shipments. High smartphone penetration, pressure on household budgets and longer replacement cycles continued to weigh on demand.

Samsung gains market share as TRANSSION retains the lead

TRANSSION accounted for 48% of smartphone shipments in Africa in 3Q26. Its shipments fell 43%, reflecting its exposure to the shrinking market for smartphones priced below $100.

Samsung recorded the smallest shipment decline among the five leading vendors, down 8%, and its market share rose to 23%. Its operator relationships and broad Galaxy A-series portfolio supported shipments. The Galaxy A07 4G and A17 4G together accounted for 56% of Samsung’s total smartphone shipments in Africa during the quarter.

Xiaomi’s shipments fell 49% as price increases across its portfolio weakened demand from channel partners and reduced its share of consumer spending.

HONOR’s shipments fell 14% YoY in 3Q26 after recording near triple-digit growth in the previous two years. Its performance in South Africa and expansion into other African markets supported that earlier growth. The decline shows how higher handset prices can slow even fast-growing vendors.

OPPO’s shipments fell 69% as it reorganized its operations as part of its integration with realme.

Tax reforms and device financing offer potential routes to recovery

Omdia expects smartphone shipments in Africa to end 2026 down 23% YoY and forecasts a further 25% decline in 2027.

“The forecast shows how heavily Africa's smartphone market depends on affordable devices and continued growth in shipments,” said Pravinkumar. “With cost pressures expected to persist into 2027, vendors face a difficult pricing challenge. They need to keep entry-level devices profitable, but passing higher component costs on to buyers risks putting smartphones beyond the reach of more households.”

Tax policy and access to financing will also shape the prospects for a recovery. Morocco reduced its smartphone import duty from 17.5% to 2.5%, illustrating how tax reform can ease cost pressures. Vodacom has introduced prepaid handset financing across all its African markets. In Nigeria, vivo is working with Credit Direct on device financing. M-KOPA continues to expand its smartphone financing model.

Pravinkumar added, “Governments, manufacturers and mobile operators all have a role in improving affordability. Closer cooperation will be essential to expand local manufacturing, make distribution more cost-effective, and give more customers access to financing. The next phase of growth depends on making connected devices affordable for a wider range of buyers.”

Average selling price (ASP) is the typical price a company receives for a single unit of a product or service, calculated by dividing total revenue by units sold. VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Eldorado Gold Corporation (TSX: ELD, NYSE: EGO) (“Eldorado” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that four tailings filter presses are now operational at its Skouries mine in northern Greece, marking another important milestone in the commissioning and ramp-up of the operation.

“With four filter presses now operational, we have achieved another important milestone in the ramp-up of Skouries,” said Christian Milau, President and Chief Executive Officer. “With this additional filtration capacity now online, we are well positioned to advance throughput and build momentum across the operation. Four operating filter presses are required to support commercial production on sulphide ore, with five required to achieve nameplate throughput. SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR), a biotechnology company developing transformative cell and exosome-based therapeutics for rare diseases, today announced that it received a Complete Response Letter (CRL) from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its resubmitted Biologics License Application (BLA) for Deramiocel, its investigational cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). The CRL states that the FDA does not consider the data sufficient to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness and cites certain other clinical deficiencies.

“We are deeply disappointed for the boys and young men living with Duchenne and their families,” said Linda Marbán, Ph.D., Capricor’s Chief Executive Officer. “Deramiocel has been studied in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, HOPE-2 and HOPE-3, both of which met their primary endpoints. We stand behind the rigor of our clinical program and the integrity of our data, and we believe the data support approval. We are reviewing the letter carefully and will share next steps once we have completed our evaluation.”

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities of approximately $198.5 million, which it believes is sufficient to fund its planned operations for at least the next 12 months. The Company is reviewing its operating costs to further extend its cash runway.

About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy

Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe, X-linked genetic disorder characterized by progressive muscle degeneration affecting the skeletal, respiratory, and cardiac muscles. It is caused by the absence of functional dystrophin, a key structural protein in muscle cells. DMD affects approximately 15,000 individuals in the United States, primarily males. Over time, deterioration of the heart muscle leads to cardiomyopathy and heart failure, the leading cause of death in DMD. There is no cure, and treatment options remain limited.

About Deramiocel

Deramiocel (CAP-1002) consists of allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cells (CDCs), a rare population of cardiac cells that have been shown in preclinical and clinical studies to exert immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic actions in the preservation of skeletal and cardiac muscle function in muscular dystrophies such as DMD. CDCs act by secreting extracellular vesicles known as exosomes, which target macrophages and alter their expression profile to adopt a healing rather than pro-inflammatory phenotype. For the treatment of DMD, Deramiocel holds Orphan Drug, RMAT and Rare Pediatric Disease designations in the U.S., and Orphan Drug and ATMP designations in Europe.

About Capricor Therapeutics

Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR) is a biotechnology company dedicated to advancing cell and exosome-based therapeutics for the treatment of rare diseases. Our lead product candidate, Deramiocel, is an allogeneic cardiac-derived cell therapy in late-stage development for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, evaluated in clinical studies for its potential to preserve skeletal and cardiac muscle function. Capricor is also advancing its proprietary StealthX™ exosome platform for the targeted delivery of oligonucleotides, proteins, and small-molecule therapeutics across a range of diseases. At Capricor, we are committed to delivering new therapies for patients with rare diseases. For more information, visit capricor.com and follow Capricor on Facebook, Instagram and X.

Through its ferries and nationwide road freight network, StraitNZ provides an essential freight and passenger link, connecting customers, communities and businesses across New Zealand’s supply chain. Services are expected to continue as normal while the transaction is completed.

HALIFAX, NS, Nov. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Isar Aerospace ("Isar") and Maritime Launch Services ("MLS") (TSX: MAXQ) (OTCQB: MAXQF) are taking the next step in advancing Canadian space capabilities with the transition of a dedicated launch complex at Spaceport Nova Scotia to Isar. This marks the moment at which Isar assumes operational responsibility for its own launch infrastructure on Canadian soil and the beginning of construction on what will become Isar's dedicated launch pad in Canada.

The handover is a key milestone in the two companies' partnership, under which Isar will develop, build and operate a dedicated launch complex, including a final assembly line and a payload preparation facility, for its Spectrum launch vehicle. First orbital launches are targeted for 2028. The announcement comes with the support of the Canadian government, reflecting shared priorities in sovereign space capability and defence cooperation.

In September this year, Isar successfully reached orbit on its second mission, becoming the first European commercial space company to deliver satellites into orbit. As the company ramps up production of its in-house-developed launch vehicle at its purpose-built factory near Munich – with capacity of 40 vehicles per year – it is also expanding its global launch site network. Spaceport Nova Scotia will be Isar's second launch site globally, and its first in North America.

"Starting construction on our launch complex at Spaceport Nova Scotia brings us a decisive step closer to launching from Canadian soil. But our ambition goes far beyond building a launch site. Together with Maritime Launch Services, we want to advance Canada's space ecosystem and establish sovereign access to orbit as a lasting national capability – one that strengthens Canada's role as a space nation and the Alliance's capabilities for years to come," said Stella Guillen, Chief Commercial Officer of Isar Aerospace.

"Today's handover marks an important step in the development of Spaceport Nova Scotia and demonstrates the strength of our multi-user spaceport model. Isar Aerospace's investment advances sovereign launch capability in Canada, strengthens cooperation between allies, and brings foreign direct investment and jobs to Nova Scotia and the communities surrounding the spaceport. It also strengthens Nova Scotia's position in the global space economy and Canada's role as a spacefaring nation," said Stephen Matier, President and CEO of Maritime Launch Services.

Spaceport Nova Scotia, developed by Maritime Launch Services Inc., is a multi-user orbital launch facility, located near the rural communities of Canso, Hazel Hill and Little Dover. Designed to support multiple launch providers and customers, its location on Nova Scotia's Atlantic coast provides over-ocean launch trajectories and access to mid- to high-inclination and polar orbits. The site will support Earth observation, communications and defence missions for government and commercial operators alike.

Isar's investment aligns directly with Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy and the Canadian Space Launch Act, both of which identify and prioritize sovereign launch capability as a national priority. As a company that designs, manufactures and operates its own launch vehicles, Isar brings integrated end-to-end launch expertise to a facility built to support Canadian and allied missions.

"Canada's sovereignty extends beyond our borders and into space. This partnership between Maritime Launch Services and Germany's Isar Aerospace is an important step toward building a sovereign space-launch capability right here in Canada. It will strengthen our national security, create new opportunities for Canadian industry, and deepen our defence cooperation with Germany. As space becomes increasingly critical to our security and our economy, Canada must have the ability to launch and protect the capabilities we depend on," said the Honourable David J. McGuinty, Minister of National Defence.

"Companies are turning to Nova Scotia to make world-class ideas into solutions, showing Nova Scotia's unique strength in the aerospace and defence sector. Congratulations to Isar and Maritime Launch Services for advancing critical launch infrastructure that will strengthen Canada's position in the global space economy and create high-value opportunities for Nova Scotians well beyond the launch pad", said the Honourable Colton LeBlanc, Minister of Growth, Development and Defence Industries, Province of Nova Scotia.

About Isar Aerospace
The European space company Isar Aerospace offers launch services for transporting small and medium-sized satellites and satellite constellations into Earth orbit. The launch vehicles used to transport these satellites are developed, manufactured, and tested almost entirely in-house. Headquartered near Munich, Germany, Isar Aerospace was founded in 2018 and has grown to over 400 employees, working across 5 international locations. Private funding from international investors provides strong backing for the company's pioneering approach to scale and industrialize launch vehicle production through vertical integration.
More information: www.isaraerospace.com

About Maritime Launch Services Inc.
Maritime Launch (TSX: MAXQ, OTCQB: MAXQF) is a Canadian-owned commercial space company based in Nova Scotia. Maritime Launch is developing Spaceport Nova Scotia, a dual-use, multi-user spaceport designed to support civil and defence-related space missions. From a single site, Spaceport Nova Scotia will enable launch vehicles to place satellites into low Earth orbit across a broad range of orbital inclinations, from 45 to 98 degrees.

MILPITAS, Calif., Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zepp Health Corporation (NYSE: ZEPP) ("Zepp", the "Company" or "we") today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial and Operating Highlights:

  • Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%.
  • Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments.
  • GAAP and adjusted net loss[1] attributable to Zepp were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million in the same period of 2025, and US$11.3 million and US$12.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. The net loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities.
  • As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million as of September 30, 2025 and US$106.3 million as of June 30, 2026.
  • Product Innovation: Launched T-Rex Dual Solar, pairing a bright AMOLED display with solar charging through both the front of the watch and its glass-ceramic back. It offers up to 25 days of battery life under typical use, and its dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation are designed for multi-day trips outdoors.
  • Software Ecosystem: Rolled out Zepp OS 6 to more existing watch models and made HYROX post-race station analysis available on more models. These updates give customers more value from the devices they already own and help build confidence in Amazfit's ongoing support for its products.

"The third quarter was a period of adjustment for us," said Wayne Huang, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Zepp Health. "Tight supply for some of our core products weighed on revenue, while unfavorable exchange rates and higher prices for memory and other chips put pressure on gross margin. The adjustments we made across our products, training software, supply, and retail are already beginning to pay off in the fourth quarter, and we are heading into the holiday season and the year ahead with momentum.

In the third quarter, global activations across the Balance family rose approximately 40% from the second quarter, driven by our new, higher-priced models. Combined global activations for Active 3 Premium and Active Max, our two US$169 models, grew approximately 35% over the same period. We also expanded our premium outdoor lineup with T-Rex Dual Solar, a watch priced at about US$650 that pairs a bright AMOLED display with dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation for multi-day trips. Through Zepp OS 6 and HYROX updates, we brought new training tools to more watches that customers already own, giving them more value from their devices.

Product availability has started to improve in some markets in the fourth quarter, including for T-Rex 3. We have also made it easier for customers to compare watches in stores. At REI, we provided materials to help shoppers compare models. Large screens are now in place at our Amazfit counters in select Best Buy stores. They make the counters easier to spot and show shoppers how our devices fit into everyday activity, training, and recovery. As more products reach store shelves, we believe we will be better positioned to meet holiday demand."

Leon Deng, Chief Financial Officer of Zepp Health, commented, "Third-quarter revenue reached US$68.3 million, up 7.5% sequentially and within our guidance range. While revenue declined 9.9% year-over-year, we continued to see encouraging momentum in our Active series. Supply constraints on certain higher-margin products, including Balance 3 and Helio Strap, limited our ability to fully capture market demand during the quarter.

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 37.4% in the previous quarter and 38.2% in the same period last year, reflecting unfavorable foreign exchange movements, continued increases in memory component costs, and supply constraints on our higher-margin products. Importantly, excluding the tariff-related benefit recorded in the second quarter, our underlying gross margin remained strong sequentially. Continued improvement in our product mix helped offset a meaningful portion of these external cost pressures, demonstrating the progress we have made in strengthening our premium product portfolio and underlying unit economics.

We continued to balance financial discipline with targeted investments to support future growth. On a sequential basis, adjusted operating expenses decreased to US$34.2 million, and adjusted operating loss narrowed to US$10.3 million. The year-over-year increase in operating expenses was primarily driven by strategic investments in new product launches, brand building, athlete partnerships, and distribution expansion. At the same time, general and administrative expenses declined, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency and manage our structural cost base.

We ended the quarter with US$99.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, while inventory declined to US$68.6 million from US$87.7 million a year earlier. We also continued to strengthen our balance sheet by extending our debt maturity profile, converting an additional US$26.6 million of short-term borrowings into longer-term obligations during the quarter. We remain committed to returning value to shareholders through our ongoing share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, we had cumulatively repurchased US$17.8 million under our US$20 million authorization, and our board of directors recently approved a one-year extension of the existing program.

Looking ahead, we expect fourth-quarter revenue to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 6% to 12%. As product availability improves and our expanded distribution channels begin contributing more meaningfully, we remain focused on translating our investments into stronger revenue growth and greater operating leverage. Despite near-term external cost pressures, we believe our improving product mix, disciplined cost management, and continued investment in the Amazfit brand are building a stronger foundation for sustainable long-term growth and profitability."

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results

Revenues

Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%. The year-over-year decline was due to the broader macroeconomic environment and a strong comparison base, as well as supply constraints on top-selling offerings, particularly Helio Strap and Balance 3. However, revenue from the Active series increased significantly year-over-year.

Gross Margin

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, supported by new product introductions including the Active series, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments. Gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 benefited from tariff refunds that the Company recorded related to duties previously remitted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"). Excluding the impact of these refunds, gross margin increased sequentially.

Research and Development Expenses

Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$11.4 million, compared with US$10.8 million and US$11.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Excluding US$0.6 million of foreign currency headwinds, research and development expenses were flat compared with the same period of 2025. We continued to invest in a series of cutting-edge products as well as new technologies, including AI, to maintain our competitive edge against our peers. At the same time, we focused on refined research and development approaches, consistently evaluating resource efficiency to optimize return on investment and productivity.

Selling and Marketing Expenses

Selling and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$18.0 million, compared with US$12.0 million and US$18.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. The US$6.0 million year-over-year increase was primarily attributable to US$1.9 million investment across online and offline channels for content refreshes, in-store displays and holiday season readiness, and US$1.5 million of launch campaigns for new products including the Balance 3, Balance Ultra and T-Rex Dual Solar. The remainder of the increase reflected US$1.4 million for marathons, Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (UTMB) and media sponsorships, and US$1.2 million related to the HYROX and new athletes partnerships.

General and Administrative Expenses

General and administrative expenses were US$5.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$7.0 million and US$6.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. We continued to streamline overhead, maintaining disciplined cost control while improving operating efficiency.

Operating Expenses

GAAP and adjusted operating expenses[2] for the third quarter of 2026 were US$35.0 million and US$34.2 million, respectively, compared with US$29.8 million and US$28.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, and US$36.0 million and US$34.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Out of the year-over-year increase of US$5.2 million in operating expenses, US$0.8 million was due to foreign currency impacts. The remaining US$4.4 million was primarily due to higher selling and marketing expenses as mentioned above. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, operating expenses decreased slightly.

Operating Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted operating results[3] were loss of US$11.1 million and loss of US$10.3 million, respectively, compared with loss of US$0.9 million and income of US$0.4 million in the same quarter of 2025. The net operating loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities, but the operating loss narrowed compared with the second quarter of 2026. 

Net Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted net loss attributable to Zepp for the third quarter of 2026 were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with GAAP and adjusted net loss of US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million for the same quarter in 2025. The US$10.9 million year-over-year increase in adjusted net loss was primarily driven by a US$6.0 million increase in selling and marketing expenses, as discussed above, followed by a US$3.2 million unfavorable foreign exchange impact. In addition, higher memory and other component costs resulted in a net US$2.7 million gross profit headwind, partially mitigated by a more favorable product mix. These unfavorable impacts were partially offset by US$1.1 million in savings from general and administrative expenses.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash were US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million and US$106.3 million as of September 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026, respectively.

The Company recorded inventory of US$68.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with US$62.4 million as of June 30, 2026 and US$87.7 million as of September 30, 2025. We will continue to manage the inventory level tightly and working capital closely.

Long-term and short-term debt levels remained flat as of September 30, 2026 compared with June 30, 2026. We remain committed to prudently managing our debt profile. Our primary objective is to maintain overall debt levels broadly stable while actively extending the maturity profile by replacing short-term borrowings with long-term debt. During the third quarter and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we successfully converted US$26.6 million and US$56.5 million, respectively, of short-term debt into long-term obligations, and we expect to continue this strategy in the coming quarters, supported by sufficient financial headroom and liquidity capacity. Since the beginning of 2023, the Company has cumulatively retired US$38.1 million of debt, and will continue to optimize its capital structure.

Share Repurchase Program Update

The Company announced in its third quarter 2021 earnings release that the board had authorized a share repurchase program of up to US$20 million through November 2022. On November 21, 2022, the board authorized a 12-month extension of the Company's share repurchase program. On November 20, 2023, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. On November 18, 2024, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 24 months. On November 22, 2026, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. Pursuant to the extended share repurchase program, the Company may repurchase its shares in the form of ADSs and/or ordinary shares through November 2027 with an aggregate value equal to the remaining balance under the share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had used US$17.8 million to repurchase approximately 2.4 million ADSs. The Company expects to fund the repurchases under the extended share repurchase program out of its existing cash balance.

Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company's management currently expects net revenues to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, which would represent an increase by approximately 6% to 12% from US$85.2 million in the fourth quarter of 2025.

This outlook is based on current market conditions and reflects the Company's current and preliminary estimates of market, operating conditions and customer demand, which are all subject to change.

About Zepp Health Corporation

Zepp Health (NYSE: ZEPP) is the technology company behind Amazfit, a global sports technology brand. Its wider portfolio includes Zepp Clarity hearing technology and Zepp Aura sleep and recovery services.

The company's vertically integrated technology platform brings together Zepp OS, wearable chipsets and biometric sensors designed in-house, and algorithms for biometric measurement and personalized guidance to enhance product performance and user experiences across devices, software and services.

Zepp Health operates as a global multi-hub organization, bringing together R&D, product, design, brand and business expertise across the Americas, Europe and Asia. These teams co-create and share responsibility for innovation, product performance and global growth.

Founded in 2013, Zepp Health has shipped more than 200 million units of smart wearable devices, with products available in more than 90 countries. Its principal office is in Gorinchem, the Netherlands. For more information, visit: www.zepp.com

Use of Non-GAAP Measures

We use adjusted net income/(loss), a non-GAAP financial measure, in evaluating our operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes. Adjusted operating expenses represent operating expenses excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Adjusted operating income/(loss) represents operating income/(loss) excluding: (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Adjusted EBIT represents net income/(loss) excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss), (vii) income tax (benefit)/expense, and (viii) interest income and interest expense. Adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation is a non-GAAP measure, which excludes (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss), and (vii) tax effects of the above non-GAAP adjustments, and is used as the numerator in computation of adjusted net income/(loss) per share and per ADS attributable to Zepp Health Corporation.

We believe that adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation help identify underlying trends in our business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain expenses that we include in net income/(loss) and net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation. We believe adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation provide useful information about our operating results, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by our management in its financial and operational decision-making.

Adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation, should not be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to net income/(loss), basic and diluted net income/(loss) per share and per ADS attributable to Zepp Health Corporation or any other measure of performance or as an indicator of our operating performance. Investors are encouraged to review the historical non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measures. Adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to ordinary shareholders, presented here may not be comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies. Other companies may calculate similarly titled measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures to our data. We encourage investors and others to review our financial information in its entirety and not rely on a single financial measure.
